items.title: Selfhosting suggestions/ideas

labels.name: :type/feature-request
labels.description: Closed at will. Feature requests are in Logseq forum https://discuss.logseq.com/

items.body:
Hi, thanks for this awesome tool, I’ve used it with docker to try to selfhost it but can’t currently find it useful (no plugins and relies on local client’s storage)

What would be amazing in my opinion is:

1. Selfhost the container and provide it with a persistent storage variable for notes folder (on the server itself or remote location, doesn’t matter)
2. When opening the web app from any client it will already be on the same notes folder
3. Support plugins on that same instance of web app, so any client will have the same experience

items.title: Hierachy files created in different ways: [Hierachy%2Ffile.md] and [Hierachy.md /Hierachy file.md]]

labels.name: :type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working. Affects daily use.

items.body:
### What happened?

Different platforms create different files in the /pages directory for hierarchies, then we have conflicts

### Reproduce the Bug

1. From Windows Logseq create hierachy **hierachy/test**
	- in folder `/pages` was created a file `hierachy%2Ftest.md`. That's Ok
2. Sync vault files (by Syncthing for example) to Android device. 
3. Edit our file **hierachy/test** on Android logseq.
	- Look at the `/pages` folder
  	- Oh, no! There is a nested folder created!
    	- /pages
        	- hierachy.md
        	- /hierachy
            	- test.md
	- Then Syncthing again to Windows machine
4. Open Windows logseq, push **Refresh**. 
	* > Page already exists with another file: /pages/hierachy%2Ftest.md, current file: /pages/hierachy/test.md

### Expected Behavior

Expect: Different platform should create files for hierarchies in the same way - with `%2F` delimiter, for example.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Desktop Platform Information

OS: Windows, Linux
Logseq: 0.7.3

### Mobile Platform Information

OS: Android 11
Logseq: 0.7.3

### Additional Context

_No response_

items.title: Slow syncing leading to disruption
items.body:
### Search first

- [X] I searched and no similar issues were found

### What Happened?

I have a habit of capturing my thoughts in logseq. As soon as a I get such a thought, I open logseq and start write it down. 

However, often, I start writing and a few seconds later whatever I have just written  gets erased or jumbled up and I have to start again, which breaks the flow. 

I think this is due to the sync feature. I start writing before the sync is finished, because I hate waiting and thoughts are perishable. 

This happens even if nothing has been written since the last sync, i.e., the markdown file is already up to date. 

On the other hand, if I have written things on another device earlier, I have to wait a long time before capturing my thoughts and waiting for the sync to finish, 10-20 seconds more. 

So sometimes I have to wait 5 seconds, sometimes 20 seconds, other times 0 seconds, etc., which breaks my flow and makes things unpredictable and annoying. 

The merge function (not sure what it’s called) where the daily journal markdown from different devices is merged also often mixes and jumbles up the order and hierarchy in which it was written. 

So all these are related to the sync feature. 

There are some others, such as pasted links not getting formatted automatically to video or tweet in mobile, the calc function being slow and buggy, etc. 

Thanks.

Open app and immediately typing rapidly

items.title: Logseq Sync Stability Issue

labels.name: :type/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement to product. Does not affect the overall basic use.

items.body:
Via: https://discuss.logseq.com/t/logseq-sync-is-not-beta-software/23112/17

Some known issues:

- Smart Merge conflicts
  - TODO -> DONE editing results in two blocks
  - Page property block is different in Smart Merge's algorithm(1 empty line diff)
  - Heading block is different in Smart Merge's algorithm(w/ or w/o prefixed `- `)
  - Adding `id::` results in two different blocks
- Current metadata is not tracked (only version number is saved)
- Not possible to revert to a specific version
- Keep logged out

items.title: Mobile logseq is having a hard time tracking files synced with icloud.

labels.name: awaiting-response
labels.description: Issue will be closed if a reply is not received

labels.name: need-to-reproduce
labels.description: More clues are required to reproduce the issue.

items.body:
### Search first

- [X] I searched and no similar issues were found

### What Happened?

I use logseq across mobile, desktop, and ipad, syncing with icloud. icloud syncing works fine, but logseq can't regularly track changes to pages or even the pages at all. 

This manifests in two specific ways:

Pretty much daily, I populate my daily journal page on desktop. Later in the day, I will go to the same page on mobile and it will be empty, until I start typing and I get a screen that shows me two conflicting versions of the page to choose from, one from logseq (which is empty) and one from disk (which is populated with what I put there on desktop that morning). I choose the version on disk, expecting this to resolve confusion for logseq. But pretty regularly, this will confuse logseq and lead to some loading screen, after which the page is blank again and I have to go through the same process. 

Relatedly, several pages that I know exist (because I've used them for a long time and they exist on both desktop and ipad) don't exist in logseq on mobile. I know this because the references to blocks in those pages appear broken only on mobile. Sure enough, when I go to the page with the missing blocks, it's empty. As mentioned above, my mobile logseq has a really hard time keeping up with the syncs, so I will start typing on the empty page and suddenly this conflicting versions page will pop up where I'm supposed to choose between the version of the page on disk (which is nonempty) and the version in logseq (which has whatever random stuff I just typed), and I will choose the populated version. At this point, the references are no longer broken. 

The reason I'm even going to the lengths of reporting this is that it's a regular, recurrent problem. The same pages keep disappearing from logseq even though they're there on disk, and it's a hassle to force a version control conflict between disk and logseq every time I have broken references.

### Reproduce the Bug

I think if this were a bug that happened broadly, I would have been able to find another issue/it would have been resolved in 0.8.18, so I don't know how to instruct you to recreate it, except by doing the following:

1. Find a page in logseq that is empty/doesn't exist, but that you are sure exists on disk
2. Start typing until you get a conflict resolution screen.

### Expected Behavior

I expect logseq to track pages that are on disk, but it doesn't seem to.

### Screenshots


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13025465/228018511-0a3d883e-bdb7-4492-987e-71254434fe59.MP4



### Desktop or Mobile Platform Information

### Additional Context

macOS 13.2.1, Desktop App v0.8.18
iPhone 13 Pro Max, iOS 16.3.1, v0.8.18

items.title: pages-metadata.edn data structure does not scale with distributed workflow

labels.name: :type/enhancement
labels.description: Enhancement to product. Does not affect the overall basic use.

items.body:
**Describe the bug**
After a few months of using git to sync Logseq on two computers, resolving merge conflicts in `pages-metadata.edn` without data loss is proving to be a challenge. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use Logseq daily on two or more computers with the same git repository as a database until `pages-metadata.edn` is ~= 3k lines. Do not put `pages-metadata.edn` in `.gitignore`.
2. Skip merging for a few days while continuing to use Logseq on both computers, making new block refs and embeds, expanding and contracting existing nodes, adding new pages, and renaming some existing pages
3. Attempt a merge
4. See hundreds of merge conflicts
6. Try accepting just one side of the merge conflicts
7. Open logseq, and see a bunch of broken references
8. Undo the merge
9. Move `pages-metadata.edn` to `pages-metadata.edn.bak` and open up logseq; observe that the file is recreated, but the created and updated dates are not accurate.

**Expected behavior**
1. If `pages-metadata.edn` is deleted and recreated, the created and updated dates should be taken from the page files metadata.
2. So far, `pages-metadata.edn` only contains name, modification date, and creation date. I would actually expect this information to be taken from and persisted in the page files themselves. If there is a performance or other reason why this should be persisted outside of the files, then the data structure that stores this information should scale to a large size and continue to function in a distributed workflow without the need for an unmanageable number of manual merge conflict resolutions, each of which could lead to data loss or corruption. 

See [`davclark`'s suggestion](https://discuss.logseq.com/t/format-pages-metadata-edn-before-saving/2506/8?u=codekiln) in logseq discuss. I'll resist the urge to research algorithmic precedent or improvise one here, but Like `davclark` I'd be happy to help in designing a data structure and algorithm. 

**Screenshots**
![image of 100s of merge conflicts](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/140930/149599099-a92c6447-3817-4a4a-a8a3-9198d7a43f0c.png)

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Mac
 - Version 0.5.8

**Additional context**
This has been discussed a bit at discuss.logseq.com: 

1. https://discuss.logseq.com/t/format-pages-metadata-edn-before-saving/2506/8?u=codekiln
2. [How important is pages-metadata.edn? - Questions & Help - Logseq](https://discuss.logseq.com/t/how-important-is-pages-metadata-edn/2896/2)
